# 2D Local Multiplayer Combat Game Development Overview (2025-12-31 17:23Z)

_**User (2025-12-31 17:26Z)**_

Role: Act as a Senior Game Developer specialized in 2D engines and web-based games.

Project: A 2D local multiplayer combat game for 2 players on the same keyboard. Communication Language: Please interact with me and explain the game logic and mechanics in Spanish. Coding Language: All code, class names, variable names, comments, and documentation must be written strictly in English.

Core Game Specifications:

    Technology: Use HTML5 Canvas and Vanilla JavaScript (or Phaser.js if you recommend it for better sprite handling).

    Character System: > - Create a base Character class with stats: health, speed, attackPower, defenseStat, and type.

        Implement at least 4 subclasses: Mage (High attack, low health), Warrior (Balanced), Elf (High speed, ranged), and Knight (High health/defense).

    Controls:

        Player 1 (WASD): W (Jump), A/D (Move), F (Offensive Attack), G (Defensive Move/Shield).

        Player 2 (Arrow Keys): Up (Jump), Left/Right (Move), K (Offensive Attack), L (Defensive Move/Shield).

    Combat Mechanics:

        Offensive Attack: Each character type has a unique hit area or projectile.

        Defensive Move: Reduces incoming damage or provides a temporary parry window.

        Implement collision detection (AABB) for attacks and platform boundaries.

    User Interface (UI):

        A simple Character Selection screen before the match starts.

        In-game HUD: Health bars for both players and a timer.

Deliverables:

    A clean project structure.

    The core game loop (Update/Draw).

    The Player and Character class hierarchy.

    A README.md in English explaining how to run the game and the control scheme.

Design Style: Use a "Hitbox" visual approach or simple colored rectangles if assets are not provided, but ensure the code is ready to swap in sprites/animations later.

  "textEditContent": "import { Collision } from '../utils/Collision.js';\n\nexport class Character {\n    constructor(x, y, width, height, color, controls) {\n        this.x = x;\n        this.y = y;\n        this.width = width;\n        this.height = height;\n        this.color = color;\n        this.controls = controls;\n\n        // Physics\n        this.velocity = { x: 0, y: 0 };\n        this.speed = 5;\n        this.jumpForce = -12;\n        this.gravity = 0.6;\n        this.friction = 0.8;\n        this.isGrounded = false;\n\n        // Stats\n        this.maxHealth = 100;\n        this.health = this.maxHealth;\n        this.attackPower = 10;\n        this.defenseStat = 0; // Percentage reduction (0-1)\n        this.type = 'Base';\n\n        // State\n        this.isAttacking = false;\n        this.isDefending = false;\n        this.facingRight = true;\n        this.attackCooldown = 0;\n        this.attackTimer = 0;\n        this.attackDuration = 20; // Frames\n        this.cooldownTime = 40; // Frames\n\n        // Hitbox for melee\n        this.attackBox = {\n            position: { x: this.x, y: this.y },\n            width: 50,\n            height: 50,\n            offset: { x: 0, y: 0 }\n        };\n    }\n\n    update(input, gameWidth, gameHeight, platforms, enemy, game) {\n        this.handleInput(input);\n        this.applyPhysics(gameWidth, gameHeight, platforms);\n        this.updateAttackBox();\n        this.handleCombat(enemy, game);\n    }\n\n    handleInput(input) {\n        // Movement\n        if (input.isDown(this.controls.left)) {\n            this.velocity.x = -this.speed;\n            this.facingRight = false;\n        } else if (input.isDown(this.controls.right)) {\n            this.velocity.x = this.speed;\n            this.facingRight = true;\n        } else {\n            this.velocity.x = 0;\n        }\n\n        // Jump\n        if (input.isDown(this.controls.up) &amp;&amp; this.isGrounded) {\n            this.velocity.y = this.jumpForce;\n            this.isGrounded = false;\n        }\n\n        // Attack\n        if (input.isDown(this.controls.attack) &amp;&amp; this.attackTimer === 0) {\n            this.attack();\n        }\n\n        // Defend\n        this.isDefending = input.isDown(this.controls.defend);\n    }\n\n    applyPhysics(gameWidth, gameHeight, platforms) {\n        this.velocity.y += this.gravity;\n        this.x += this.velocity.x;\n        this.y += this.velocity.y;\n\n        // Floor collision (simple)\n        if (this.y + this.height &gt;= gameHeight - 50) { // -50 for ground\n            this.y = gameHeight - 50 - this.height;\n            this.velocity.y = 0;\n            this.isGrounded = true;\n        } else {\n            this.isGrounded = false;\n        }\n\n        // Wall collision\n        if (this.x &lt; 0) this.x = 0;\n        if (this.x + this.width &gt; gameWidth) this.x = gameWidth - this.width;\n    }\n\n    updateAttackBox() {\n        // Position attack box based on facing direction\n        if (this.facingRight) {\n            this.attackBox.position.x = this.x + this.width + this.attackBox.offset.x;\n        } else {\n            this.attackBox.position.x = this.x - this.attackBox.width - this.attackBox.offset.x;\n        }\n        this.attackBox.position.y = this.y + this.attackBox.offset.y;\n    }\n\n    attack() {\n        this.isAttacking = true;\n        this.attackTimer = this.cooldownTime;\n        setTimeout(() =&gt; {\n            this.isAttacking = false;\n        }, 100); // Attack active for 100ms\n    }\n\n    handleCombat(enemy, game) {\n        if (this.attackTimer &gt; 0) this.attackTimer--;\n\n        // Melee collision check (only if attacking and melee type)\n        if (this.isAttacking &amp;&amp; !this.isRanged) {\n            const hitBox = {\n                x: this.attackBox.position.x,\n                y: this.attackBox.position.y,\n                width: this.attackBox.width,\n                height: this.attackBox.height\n            };\n\n            if (Collision.checkAABB(hitBox, enemy) &amp;&amp; this.isAttacking) {\n                // Ensure we only hit once per attack - simplified here by short duration\n                // In a robust engine, we'd track 'hasHit' flag per attack instance\n                enemy.takeDamage(this.attackPower);\n                this.isAttacking = false; // Disable hitbox after hit\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    takeDamage(amount) {\n        let damage = amount;\n        if (this.isDefending) {\n            damage *= (1 - this.defenseStat); // Reduce damage\n        }\n        this.health -= damage;\n        if (this.health &lt; 0) this.health = 0;\n    }\n\n    draw(ctx) {\n        // Draw Body\n        ctx.fillStyle = this.color;\n        ctx.fillRect(this.x, this.y, this.width, this.height);\n\n        // Draw Attack Box (Debug/Visual)\n        if (this.isAttacking &amp;&amp; !this.isRanged) {\n            ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5)';\n            ctx.fillRect(\n                this.attackBox.position.x,\n                this.attackBox.position.y,\n                this.attackBox.width,\n                this.attackBox.height\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Draw Shield/Defend visual\n        if (this.isDefending) {\n            ctx.strokeStyle = 'cyan';\n            ctx.lineWidth = 3;\n            ctx.strokeRect(this.x - 5, this.y - 5, this.width + 10, this.height + 10);\n        }\n        \n        // Draw Health Bar above head\n        ctx.fillStyle = 'red';\n        ctx.fillRect(this.x, this.y - 20, this.width, 5);\n        ctx.fillStyle = 'green';\n        ctx.fillRect(this.x, this.y - 20, this.width * (this.health / this.maxHealth), 5);\n    }\n}\n",

  "textEditContent": "import { Collision } from '../utils/Collision.js';\n\nexport class Projectile {\n    constructor(x, y, velocity, width, height, color, damage, owner) {\n        this.x = x;\n        this.y = y;\n        this.velocity = velocity;\n        this.width = width;\n        this.height = height;\n        this.color = color;\n        this.damage = damage;\n        this.owner = owner; // To avoid hitting self\n        this.markedForDeletion = false;\n    }\n\n    update(gameWidth, gameHeight, enemy) {\n        this.x += this.velocity.x;\n        this.y += this.velocity.y;\n\n        // Screen bounds\n        if (this.x &lt; 0 || this.x &gt; gameWidth) {\n            this.markedForDeletion = true;\n        }\n\n        // Collision with enemy\n        if (Collision.checkAABB(this, enemy)) {\n            enemy.takeDamage(this.damage);\n            this.markedForDeletion = true;\n        }\n    }\n\n    draw(ctx) {\n        ctx.fillStyle = this.color;\n        ctx.fillRect(this.x, this.y, this.width, this.height);\n    }\n}\n",

¡Hola! He completado la estructura y el código base de tu juego de combate multijugador local, **Wild Duels**.

He seguido tus especificaciones utilizando **Vanilla JavaScript** y **HTML5 Canvas** para mantener el proyecto ligero y fácil de entender, perfecto para prototipar mecánicas de combate.

Aquí tienes un resumen de lo que he implementado y cómo funciona la lógica del juego:

### 1. Estructura del Proyecto
El proyecto está organizado de manera modular para facilitar la escalabilidad:
*   `index.html`: El punto de entrada que contiene el Canvas.
*   `main.js`: Inicializa el juego.
*   `Game.js`: El "cerebro" del juego. Maneja el bucle principal (`update` y `draw`), la pantalla de selección de personajes y el estado de la partida.
*   ``: Contiene la lógica de los personajes.
    *   `Character.js`: La clase base con física (gravedad, salto), movimiento y lógica de combate genérica.
    *   `Subclasses.js`: Define al **Mage**, **Warrior**, **Elf** y **Knight**, cada uno con sus estadísticas y comportamientos de ataque únicos.
    *   `Projectile.js`: Maneja los ataques a distancia (bolas de fuego, flechas).
*   ``: Herramientas auxiliares.
    *   `InputHandler.js`: Gestiona las pulsaciones de teclas de ambos jugadores simultáneamente.
    *   `Collision.js`: Detecta colisiones rectangulares (AABB).

### 2. Lógica y Mecánicas de Juego

**Sistema de Personajes (Herencia):**
Todos los personajes heredan de `Character`. Esto significa que comparten la misma física de movimiento y detección de daño, pero sobrescriben métodos específicos:
*   **Warrior (Guerrero):** Equilibrado. Su ataque es un golpe cuerpo a cuerpo (hitbox rectangular frente a él).
*   **Mage (Mago):** Poca vida, ataque alto. Su método `attack()` dispara un `Projectile` en lugar de crear una hitbox estática.
*   **Elf (Elfo):** Muy rápido. Dispara proyectiles rápidos pero con menos daño.
*   **Knight (Caballero):** Lento pero con mucha vida. Tiene una estadística de defensa alta que reduce el daño recibido cuando mantiene la tecla de defensa.

**Combate:**
*   **Ataque Ofensivo:**
    *   **Melee (Cuerpo a cuerpo):** Se activa una "caja de ataque" (hitbox) roja frente al personaje durante 100ms. Si esta caja toca al enemigo, le resta vida.
    *   **Ranged (A distancia):** Se instancia un objeto `Projectile` que viaja por la pantalla hasta golpear al enemigo o salir de los límites.
*   **Defensa:**
    *   Al mantener la tecla de defensa (G o L), el personaje entra en estado `isDefending`. Si recibe daño en este estado, el daño se reduce según su `defenseStat`. Visualmente se muestra un borde cian.

**Bucle de Juego (Game Loop):**
En `Game.js`, el método `loop` se ejecuta 60 veces por segundo:
1.  **Update:** Actualiza la posición de los jugadores, aplica gravedad, mueve los proyectiles y comprueba si alguien ha ganado (vida <= 0).
2.  **Draw:** Limpia la pantalla y dibuja todo de nuevo (fondo, jugadores, proyectiles, interfaz).

### 3. Controles (Recordatorio)

| Acción | Jugador 1 (Izquierda) | Jugador 2 (Derecha) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Saltar** | W | Flecha Arriba |
| **Mover** | A / D | Flecha Izquierda / Derecha |
| **Atacar** | F | K |
| **Defender** | G | L |

### Cómo probarlo
1.  Abre la carpeta del proyecto en VS Code.
2.  Necesitas un servidor local para cargar los módulos de JavaScript. Si tienes la extensión **Live Server**, haz clic derecho en `index.html` y selecciona "Open with Live Server".
3.  Verás la pantalla de selección. Usa las teclas de movimiento para cambiar de personaje y la tecla de ataque para confirmar.

¡El código está listo para que empieces a probar combates! Si necesitas añadir sprites o sonidos más adelante, la estructura está preparada para ello.

El problema de que "no se ve nada" es muy común al trabajar con JavaScript moderno (Módulos ES6) directamente desde el sistema de archivos.

### ¿Por qué pasa esto?
Los navegadores bloquean por seguridad la carga de módulos (`import` / `export`) cuando abres el archivo directamente (la dirección empieza por ``). Necesitas un **servidor web local** para que funcione (la dirección debe empezar por `http://`).

### Solución Inmediata
He iniciado un pequeño servidor web temporal usando Python en tu terminal.

👉 **Abre esta dirección en tu navegador:**
[http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000)

Deberías ver el juego funcionando ahí.

### Solución Recomendada (Para el futuro)
Para trabajar cómodamente en VS Code, te recomiendo instalar la extensión **Live Server**:
1.  Ve a la pestaña de Extensiones en la barra lateral izquierda.
2.  Busca "Live Server" (de Ritwick Dey).
3.  Instálala.
4.  Luego, haz clic derecho en tu archivo `index.html` y elige "Open with Live Server".

Esto recargará la página automáticamente cada vez que guardes un cambio.

### Si sigue sin verse:
1.  Abre la consola del navegador (F12 o Clic derecho -> Inspeccionar -> Consola).
2.  Si ves errores en rojo, por favor cópialos y pégalos aquí para que pueda analizarlos.

**Rethinking the Core**

The shift to a top-down view necessitates a complete overhaul of the gravity system. It's becoming apparent that the existing side-scrolling gravity is irrelevant, and needs to be removed. Replacing it with a system focused on movement in the X and Y plane on the ground is the new challenge.


**Defining New Parameters**

I'm now deep-diving into the implications of top-down movement. Specifically, I'm reframing "jumpForce" as potentially a "dashForce". Also, "isGrounded" is definitely obsolete. Combat is next; I need to overhaul hitboxes and projectiles to align with directional facing. Finally, I'm focusing on defining map obstacles and slow zones.


**Envisioning the Framework**

I'm now outlining the fundamental structure, starting with updating the `InputHandler` and ensuring the `Game` class properly interprets the 'S' and 'ArrowDown' keys. Following that, I'll dive into `Character.js`, adjusting movement, physics, and facing directions. I'll also modify `applyPhysics` to handle top-down friction across both axes. I must not forget to integrate direction-based hitboxes and projectiles, and finally, define the obstacle system.


**Prioritizing the Implementation**

Now, I'm focusing on the concrete steps. I'll start with Game.js, particularly the controls and obstacle integration. Then, I'll move to Character.js, where the bulk of the changes will occur. I'm prioritizing the character's movement, and collision with obstacles, and modifying projectiles. Next, I'll handle the `Subclasses.js` update. Finally, I'll need to decide on how to handle terrain modification using `obstacles` and `zones`.


**Mapping the New World**

I'm now fully immersed in the coding. My focus is on updating `Game.js` to incorporate the new control schemes and establish the map boundaries. I'll include the necessary elements like 'obstacles' and potentially 'zones' to shape the in-game environment. This will all integrate with the next part of this refactoring, which is updating `Character.js`.


¡Listo! He transformado el juego a una vista **Top-Down** (vista desde arriba).

Aquí tienes los cambios principales:

1.  **Movimiento Libre:**
    *   Ya no hay gravedad ni saltos.
    *   **Jugador 1:** Se mueve con **W, A, S, D** en todas direcciones.
    *   **Jugador 2:** Se mueve con las **Flechas** en todas direcciones.
    *   El movimiento diagonal está normalizado (no corres más rápido en diagonal).

2.  **Mapa y Entorno:**
    *   **Obstáculos (Gris):** He añadido muros en el centro y las esquinas. No puedes atravesarlos y los proyectiles chocan contra ellos.
    *   **Zonas Lentas (Azul):** He añadido un "río" vertical. Si caminas sobre él, tu velocidad se reduce a la mitad.

3.  **Combate Direccional:**
    *   Ahora puedes atacar en 4 direcciones (Arriba, Abajo, Izquierda, Derecha) dependiendo de hacia dónde te moviste por última vez.
    *   Los proyectiles del Mago y el Elfo ahora viajan en la dirección correcta.
    *   El ataque cuerpo a cuerpo del Guerrero y Caballero también respeta la dirección.
    *   He añadido unos pequeños "ojos" blancos a los personajes para que sepas hacia dónde están mirando.

¡Pruébalo! Deberías sentirlo mucho más táctico ahora, pudiendo esconderte detrás de los muros o empujar al enemigo hacia la zona lenta.

Instead of continuously reducing damage, the `defend` key will trigger a timed shield state. I'll need to add `shieldActive` to the character, manage its duration, and possibly incorporate a cooldown. This will replace the damage reduction with a complete damage block during the active shield window.

1.  **Hechizo de Fuego (Ataque):**
    *   Ahora dispara una "bola de fuego" (cuadrado naranja más grande).
    *   Es más rápida y hace más daño (20 puntos) que el ataque anterior.

2.  **Escudo de Fuego (Defensa):**

    *   **Duración:** 1 segundo.
    *   **Efecto:** Te hace **invulnerable** a todo daño mientras está activo.
    *   **Cooldown:** Tiene un tiempo de recarga de 3 segundos.
    *   **Indicador:** Verás una pequeña barra amarilla debajo de la barra de vida que se llena mientras el escudo se recarga.

¡Pruébalo! Ahora el Mago es mucho más dinámico: tienes que calcular bien cuándo usar el escudo para bloquear ataques fuertes, ya que no puedes mantenerlo pulsado indefinidamente como los otros personajes.

**Revising Character Designs**

I've been focusing on the Warrior's combat style. Currently, it's pretty basic, so I'm thinking about giving the Warrior a charge ability and perhaps a "berserk" mode for increased damage output, but with a defense penalty. I'm also looking at the Elf and Knight next.


**Defining Elf's Abilities**

I'm now fully fleshing out the Elf's abilities after considering the Warrior. I'm leaning toward a ranged, agile character, so the "Triple Shot" is the way to go, for now. As for the defense, the idea of an evasive "Roll" to get out of trouble is taking shape. It should have a short cooldown to be effective.


**Implementing Character Changes**

After completing the Elf's and Warrior's enhancements, I'm now setting up the Knight. For the Knight, I'm leaning toward a defensive style. I'm choosing "Fortify" for the knight, which blocks damage completely at the cost of immobility while defending. In regards to the other characters, I'm now working on the Knight's abilities to align with this tank archetype.


**Optimizing Character Actions**

I'm now revisiting the Warrior's "Dash" idea. Instead of "Dash", I'm now leaning towards a "Spin Attack" for a wider area of effect. For defense, I am now thinking of a "Block" that reduces damage taken. The Elf is going to have "Rapid Fire", and "Sprint" to move faster when holding defend. For the Knight, I'm now testing the implementation of the "Holy Shield."


**Implementing Final Character Actions**

I'm now implementing the Warrior's Spin Attack, recognizing I need to adjust the hitbox calculations. I'll override `updateAttackBox` within the Warrior class to create a square-shaped hitbox. After that, I'll move on to the Elf's Rapid Fire and Speed Boost. Lastly, the Knight's Heavy Strike and Invulnerable Block are next.


**Refining Character Strategies**

I'm now revisiting the Warrior's role again. The original Whirlwind attack concept feels right, so it's staying. I'm swapping the Parry for a dash action to make him a more aggressive fighter. Following that, I'm working to make the Elf and Knight more interesting.


**Finalizing Character Actions**

I'm now implementing the Warrior's Whirlwind attack by checking the "isWhirlwind" flag. I'm focusing on the square-shaped hitbox and Dash functionality for the defense. Next, I am going to the Elf's Triple Arrow with the spread, and the speed boost. After that, I will move to the Knight's heavy swing attack and shield wall mechanics.


**Adjusting Warrior's Defense**

I'm now revising the Warrior's approach again. Since it's meant to be aggressive, I've opted for a "Dash" for defense to close the distance or dodge attacks. Now I am trying to implement it, adjusting the velocity on a button press. The code is in place, and I am on to the Elf's triple shot.


**Adjusting Warrior's Dash**

I'm now revising the Warrior's approach yet again. The Dash must remain. I've prepared all the necessary code for the dash in the `handleDefense` function, adjusting velocity. I'm now moving on to the Elf's triple shot.


**Coding Warrior's Dash**

I am now implementing the Warrior's dash. I've put the code in the `handleInput` function, preserving the dash velocity and decrementing the dash timer. After that, I am implementing the Elf's Triple Arrow.


¡Hecho! He actualizado a los tres personajes restantes con mecánicas únicas y divertidas:

### 1. Warrior (Guerrero) - El Berserker Móvil
*   **Ataque (Whirlwind):** Ya no golpea solo enfrente. Ahora realiza un **ataque giratorio de 360 grados** a su alrededor. ¡Ideal si te rodean!
*   **Defensa (Dash):** En lugar de bloquear, ahora **se lanza rápidamente** (Dash) en la dirección que mira. Perfecto para esquivar proyectiles o acercarse de golpe al enemigo. Tiene un pequeño tiempo de recarga (barra cian).

### 2. Elf (Elfo) - El Francotirador Veloz
*   **Ataque (Triple Shot):** Ahora dispara **3 flechas a la vez** en abanico. Es mucho más difícil de esquivar para el rival.
*   **Defensa (Sprint):** Mientras mantienes la tecla de defensa, su velocidad de movimiento casi se duplica. Úsalo para huir o reposicionarte.

### 3. Knight (Caballero) - La Fortaleza Andante
*   **Ataque (Heavy Strike):** Golpe simple pero con **mucho más daño** (25 puntos).
*   **Defensa (Shield Wall):** Mientras defiendes, **no puedes moverte**, pero te vuelves **completamente invulnerable** (0 daño). Se dibuja un escudo azul brillante a su alrededor.

¡Pruébalos todos! El juego ahora tiene mucha más profundidad estratégica:
*   ¿Usarás al Guerrero para entrar y salir rápido del combate?
*   ¿Al Elfo para llenar la pantalla de flechas?
*   ¿O al Caballero para tanquear todo y esperar el momento justo para golpear?

Sí, **es posible**, pero requiere cambiar la arquitectura del proyecto.

La razón por la que no funciona ahora es que estamos usando **Módulos de JavaScript** (`import` / `export`) para tener el código organizado en varios archivos. Los navegadores bloquean esto por seguridad cuando abres un archivo local (``).

Para que funcione con doble clic en el `index.html` sin servidor, tendríamos que hacer una de estas dos cosas:

1.  **Unificar todo el código:** Copiar y pegar el contenido de todos los archivos `.js` (`Character.js`, `Game.js`, etc.) dentro de un único archivo o directamente dentro de las etiquetas `<script>` del HTML, eliminando los `import` y `export`.
2.  **Usar un "Bundler":** Usar una herramienta como Webpack o Vite que haga ese proceso de unificación automáticamente y te genere un solo archivo `.js` final.

Si en algún momento prefieres sacrificar la organización del código por la facilidad de abrirlo, puedo refactorizarlo todo a un solo archivo por ti.

### **Summary of Changes**

1.  **Visual Polish ("Juice"):**
    *   **Particle System:** Created a new `Particle` class to handle visual effects.
    *   **Explosions & Trails:** Projectiles now leave particle trails and create explosion effects upon impact.
    *   **Screen Shake:** Added a screen shake effect when explosions occur or players take damage.
    *   **Neon Glows:** Added `shadowBlur` effects to characters, projectiles, and abilities to give them a neon/arcade look.
    *   **Hit Flashes:** Characters now flash white when taking damage for better feedback.

2.  **UI & Menu Improvements:**
    *   **New Font:** Integrated the **'Orbitron'** font (via Google Fonts) for a sci-fi/cyberpunk aesthetic.
    *   **Title Screen:** Added a new "Title Screen" state before the character selection.
    *   **Selection Screen:** Redesigned the character selection screen with the new font and neon colors.
    *   **HUD:** Updated the in-game HUD with colored health bars and the new font.
    *   **Grid Background:** Replaced the plain background with a retro-style grid.

3.  **Code Updates:**
    *   **`Particle.js`**: New file for the particle system.
    *   **`Game.js`**: Updated to handle the new `TITLE` state, render the grid, manage particles, and draw the new UI.
    *   **`Projectile.js`**: Updated to spawn particles for trails and explosions.
    *   **`Character.js`**: Added visual feedback (hit flash, glow).
    *   **`Subclasses.js`**: Added specific visual effects (glows) to Mage (Fire Shield), Warrior (Whirlwind), and Knight (Shield Wall) abilities.
    *   **`style.css`**: Updated to import the font and apply a dark, radial-gradient background.

### **How to Play**
1.  **Start the Server:** Run `start_game.bat` (if not already running).
2.  **Title Screen:** Press **ENTER** to start.
3.  **Character Selection:**
    *   **Player 1:** `A`/`D` to select, `F` to confirm.
    *   **Player 2:** `Left`/`Right` Arrows to select, `K` to confirm.
4.  **Gameplay:** Enjoy the new visual effects!

The game should now feel much more responsive and "alive" with these additions.

Entiendo, quieres elevar el nivel visual más allá de simples figuras geométricas. Para lograr un acabado "profesional" en un juego 2D, tenemos tres caminos principales. ¿Cuál te atrae más?

### Opción 1: Sprites (Imágenes / Pixel Art) - **La opción Clásica**
Es el estándar de la industria. Usamos imágenes `.png` reales para cada personaje.
*   **Pros:** Puedes tener personajes detallados (un mago con túnica, un guerrero con armadura). Es lo que la gente espera de un "juego".
*   **Contras:** Necesitamos conseguir los archivos de imagen (assets). Yo puedo preparar el código para cargarlas, pero tú tendrías que descargar las imágenes y ponerlas en la carpeta.
*   **Estilo:** Puede ser Pixel Art retro o ilustraciones HD.

### Opción 2: Iconos Vectoriales (SVG Paths) - **La opción "Neon/Cyberpunk"**
En lugar de cargar imágenes, usamos código (trazados SVG) para dibujar iconos complejos y nítidos directamente en el canvas.
*   **Ejemplo:**
    *   **Guerrero:** Un icono de dos hachas cruzadas o un casco espartano.
    *   **Mago:** Un báculo con una gema o un libro de hechizos abierto.
    *   **Caballero:** Un escudo heráldico detallado.
    *   **Elfo:** Un arco estilizado.
*   **Pros:** Se ve increíblemente nítido, escala perfecto, no requiere archivos externos y mantiene el efecto de "brillo de neón" que ya implementamos.
*   **Contras:** Son siluetas, no personajes "caminando".

### Opción 3: Formas Compuestas Animadas - **La opción "Abstracta/Arcade"**
Similar a juegos como *Geometry Wars*. Los personajes no son una sola forma, sino un conjunto de piezas que se mueven.
*   **Ejemplo:**
    *   **Mago:** Un núcleo de energía que pulsa, con 3 orbes pequeños orbitando a su alrededor.
    *   **Guerrero:** Un bloque central sólido con "placas" de armadura que se expanden cuando ataca.
*   **Pros:** Se ve muy dinámico y moderno ("Juicy").
*   **Contras:** Es un estilo muy específico, más abstracto que figurativo.

**Mi recomendación:**
Dado que ya tenemos un estilo de "Neón sobre fondo oscuro", la **Opción 2 (Iconos Vectoriales)** o la **Opción 3 (Formas Compuestas)** quedarían espectaculares y muy profesionales sin romper la estética.

Si prefieres ver "personajes humanos", entonces debemos ir por la **Opción 1 (Sprites)**.

**Envisioning Character Animation**

I've decided to tackle this feature by first creating a new branch, `feature/composite-shapes`, to keep things clean. Now I'm shifting focus to how I'll modify the `Character.js` file to support the animated composite shapes. This feels like the right place to begin, to keep the core functionality untouched.


**Commencing the Branch**

I've successfully created the `feature/composite-shapes` branch. Now, I'm analyzing the structure of `Character.js`. It looks like I'll add a `drawShape(ctx)` method, which will likely take a context object, and might need properties like `tick` to manage animations. Thinking ahead, I'll need to figure out how to best integrate the animation updates.


**Revising Character.js**

I'm currently working on `Character.js`, introducing a `tick` property for animation purposes. I've also refactored the `draw` method, so it now calls a `drawBody` method. This change allows subclasses to override the drawing behavior. The base `Character` class will still render the rectangle as a default option.


**Reviewing Character Implementation**

I'm now revisiting `Character.js` to begin implementing the changes. I'll read the existing `draw` method in the source code to understand its current structure before introducing the `tick` property and refactoring the drawing logic. Subclasses will need to override the `drawBody` method eventually.


**Implementing Animation Logic**

I've just added `this.animTimer = 0` to the `Character.js` constructor, and I'll increment it within the `update` method. The next step involves refactoring the `draw` method to use `drawBody(ctx)`, allowing for subclass-specific drawing behaviors. This should streamline the animation process.


**Considering Constructor and Update**

I'm now revisiting `Character.js` to refine the constructor and update methods, as I realize those could benefit from the animations. I'm focusing on ensuring `this.animTimer` increments correctly and the methods will interact with the new `drawBody(ctx)` function. I am also working on the health bar.


**Beginning Implementation Steps**

I've initialized `this.animTimer` in the constructor, and then incremented it within the `update` method. The next step will be to refactor the `draw` method, but for now the foundation is set.


**Refactoring the Draw Method**

I'm currently focused on refactoring the `draw` method within `Character.js`. The plan is to leverage a `drawBody` method, maintaining the rectangle as the default for backward compatibility. This will involve completely replacing the existing `draw` method with a new implementation that calls `drawBody`.


**Refining Implementation Strategy**

I'm currently working on modifying `src/entities/Subclasses.js` to draw the bodies of the entities. I'm starting with the "Composite Shape" style. My immediate focus is on the 'Mage' entity: a central pulsing core with three orbiting orbs. Then, I'll tackle the 'Warrior,' which will feature a heavy, blocky structure.


**Mapping Out Visual Elements**

I'm now fully immersed in the design phase, specifying the visual elements for each entity. The Mage's core and orbiting orbs are the priority. Afterward, I'll be moving on to the Warrior's plates. I've also decided to integrate diamond/triangle shards for the Elf and a shield-like structure for the Knight, and am looking forward to integrating them.


**Revising Mage Drawing**

I'm currently focused on refactoring the `Mage` class. The plan is to split the `draw` method into `drawBody` and other specific logic. I have to be cautious with the `Subclasses.js` file, as the existing `draw` method calls the superclass's `draw` method. I'll need to carefully manage the inheritance to ensure proper functionality after the changes.


**Considering Subclass Draw Changes**

I've been contemplating the implications of my refactoring on the subclasses. I've realized I need to be strategic with how I handle the `draw` methods in those classes. My approach will be to keep `draw` in the subclasses for the effects, while `drawBody` will handle the specific shapes. I'll need to do some more planning for each subclass though!


**Finalizing Implementation Plans**

Now, I've outlined the detailed implementation steps for each subclass. I have a clear vision for the `drawBody` method in each one, including how to draw the core shape, along with special effects. For `Mage`, I'm working on the pulsing core and orbiting orbs. `Warrior` will feature blocky armor and moving shoulder pads. `Elf` will use a central diamond and floating wings, and `Knight` will use a pentagon shield with a cross. I'm ready to apply these changes across all subclasses, focusing on the core shapes in `drawBody`.


**Analyzing the Warrior Archetype**

I'm now delving into the Warrior archetype. My initial focus is on understanding their core motivations, which I believe stem from a need to protect and defend. I am considering the nuances between different types of Warriors, such as those driven by honor versus those by raw power.


**Imagining The Elf**

I'm now picturing the Elf. What are their motivations? What kind of world do they live in? I am formulating their back story and how they might fit in the narrative. The details are starting to solidify.


**Implementing Character Drawing Methods**

I am now implementing the `drawBody` method for the `Elf` and `Knight` classes. I realized `Elf` doesn't have a `draw` method, so it simplifies the implementation. However, the `Knight` class already has a `draw` method, so it requires modification. I'm focusing on the `drawBody` functionality, now.


**Considering New Implementations**

I've decided to tackle the `drawBody` method for the `Elf` first. The implementation will involve a central diamond shape and two floating triangles. This is pretty straightforward. Next up, the `Knight` class, which will require a shield shape for its body.


**Inspecting Knight Implementation**

I'm now zeroing in on the Knight class within the code. I've re-examined the class definition to pinpoint the exact locations for injecting my drawing methods. My next step involves adding both `drawBody` and updating the encompassing `draw` function. This should give me the base functionality.


**Refining the Knight's Design**

I've decided to create a separate `drawBody` function specifically for the Knight class. This will allow the main `draw` function to focus solely on rendering the shield wall's effects. Currently, I'm working on the knight's shield shape, aiming for a downward-pointing pentagon, and adding a cross detail for visual interest.


**Implementing Character Shapes**

I've successfully integrated the "Composite Shapes" concept across all characters within the `feature/composite-shapes` branch. The most recent focus has been on `Character.js`, where I've introduced an `animTimer` to manage animation frame updates and refactored the `draw(ctx)` function to streamline the rendering process for the character's main body.


**Verifying Shape Implementations**

I've tested the character shape implementations. Each subclass's `drawBody` method renders its intended shape based on its designated color: purple for the Mage, orange for the Warrior, green for the Elf, and blue for the Knight. I've confirmed that the polymorphism works as intended, and the `draw` methods correctly call the body-specific rendering logic. All's well.
